week01_numerical_foundations.title: Cavity validation across all seven Ghia Reynolds numbers

blocks.text: The first worked cavity remains the introduction. Extend its validation to Re = 100, 400, 1000, 3200, 5000, 7500 and 10000. With cavity width L, lid speed U and kinematic viscosity nu, Re = UL/nu. The reference is a square cavity with a discontinuous moving lid, not a Gaussian-regularized or deep-cavity problem.
What the benchmark actually supplies

Ghia, Ghia and Shin (1982), Tables I and II, supply 17 samples of u/U on x/L = 0.5 and 17 of v/U on y/L = 0.5 at each Re. These are profiles, not a dense two-dimensional velocity/pressure field. The shared module flowmllab/ghia.py is now the single source for the seven cases; the notebook shows every case.

Retain these printed entries. Report an unfiltered score and a second score using the predeclared mask. No replacement value is invented, and the mask is not selected to make a model look good. A flag is a disclosed sensitivity policy, not an author-issued erratum.
A reliable error definition
For N retained coordinates, use a shared profile norm and RMS in lid-speed units:

Here hats denote predictions and unhatted values the reference samples. Define the v error analogously. Interpolate to the original reference coordinates. Do not divide by the local velocity at a zero crossing or extrapolate interior samples to a wall.

Source: Ghia et al., JCP 48 (1982), 387-411, DOI 10.1016/0021-9991(82)90058-4. Data and anomaly policy: references/ghia/README.md. Follow-on lesson: notebooks/week04/W4_Lab5_All_Re_Ghia_Validation.ipynb.

week01_numerical_foundations.title: From a comparison plot to a validation decision

blocks.text: A selectable Reynolds number does not certify a solver. New Lab 7 now supplies actual CFD at all four higher Ghia Reynolds numbers on 128, 256 and 512 cells per side. Matched low-Re and additional training fields complete 45 solutions. All pass independent discrete-equation checks; material high-Re mesh sensitivity remains.
Three independent questions
1. Have the discrete equations been solved? Check continuity, Poisson/momentum residuals and a steady residual expressed per unit physical time. A small update at a tiny time step can be misleading.

2. Does refinement change the answer? Compare at least three grids and halve the time step at fixed physics. Track both signed centreline profiles, primary/secondary vortices and corner resolution. A steady gate alone is not mesh convergence.

3. Is the reference matched? Match Re, geometry, lid profile, normalization and observable. Centreline velocity agreement does not validate pressure reconstructed from momentum or every point of a two-dimensional field.
Required engineering table

rows: Re, grid, time step, convection scheme, wall/lid treatment
Steps, physical time, steady residual and continuity norm
E_u, E_v, RMS/U, printed-data sensitivity and vortex position
Admit / reject / unavailable, with a stated reason

blocks.text: Start with the retained Re = 400 and 1000 cases at 32, 64 and 128 cells. Fill the table before attempting higher Re. If a solution remains unsteady or a grid is unresolved, keep that outcome visible and do not convert its time average into an unqualified steady benchmark.

Exercise: identify the largest signed near-wall error, explain why an aggregate norm may hide it, and calculate both masked and unfiltered errors for the three suspicious entries. Use the new field/hash manifest in Lab 7; distinguish a converged discrete solution from a mesh-independent physical reference.

week01_2_pressure_velocity.title: Extending SIMPLE, PISO and PIMPLE to the seven-Re benchmark

blocks.text: The experimental wrapper now accepts all Ghia cases: Re = 100, 400, 1000, 3200, 5000, 7500, 10000. The original Re = 100 qualification and the retained Re = 400/1000 results are preserved. Accepting a configuration changes the available experiment, not its validation status.
Separate coupling, spatial error and temporal error

At matched Re, mesh, lid treatment and spatial discretization, coupling algorithms can be compared by pressure solves and elapsed time needed to reach the same physical accuracy. If convection or resolution differs, the difference cannot be assigned to the pressure-correction algorithm alone.

SIMPLE iterations are not physical time steps. PISO and PIMPLE may advance physical time, but convergence of inner corrections does not establish time-step accuracy. Repeat with a smaller time step and compare a physical observable at the same time; for a steady study, also verify stationarity.

rows: E_u and E_v at Ghia coordinates
Tests both velocity components with a common norm denominator
Reveals displaced extrema and boundary-layer resolution
Separates a solved discrete problem from a small step update
Separates discretization error from coupling convergence
Ghia velocity samples do not supply an independent pressure reference

blocks.text: Use the existing 32/64/128-cell Re = 400/1000 runs first. For each of the four higher Re values, prepare the same table and leave uncomputed entries blank. Explicit central-convection time stepping can fail on an unsuitable grid; report the failure, refine or change the qualified discretization, and retain the reason.

Canonical samples and three predeclared anomaly masks: references/ghia/README.md. Experimental API: flowmllab/pressure_velocity_experiments.py. Every score also has an unfiltered printed-data version. The optional new-solve notebook cell is off by default.

week01_2_pressure_velocity.title: Exercise: a defensible high-Re acceptance gate

blocks.text: Before a run

Declare the discrete equations, grid sequence, time-step sequence, lid-corner convention and stopping tolerances. Record a reference-only row for every Re, even when no field exists. Decide which observable will establish convergence before looking at the desired answer.
After a run

Interpolate u at x/L = 0.5 and v at y/L = 0.5 using the actual mesh coordinates. Compare at the original Ghia nodes. Report RMS in U units and relative L2 using the entire reference profile norm, both screened and unfiltered. Plot signed differences. Explain any mismatch between a small residual and poor reference agreement.
Required submission

Submit one table with Re, algorithm, grid, time step, runtime, pressure solves, continuity, steady residual, E_u, E_v and an acceptance decision. Add two physical-profile plots and one mesh-sensitivity plot per chosen Re. Explain why a failed high-Re case must not be silently included in the Week 4 neural training set.

Compare algorithm timings only after the reference/accuracy gate is matched. Warm up numerical libraries and repeat timings; count linear solves and residual evaluations. A smaller iteration count can still cost more time per iteration. Record machine and thread settings.

The new seven-Re centreline neural exercise is in Week 4 Lab 6. It uses sparse published samples and cannot replace the full-field CFD acceptance process described here. Ghia et al. (1982): DOI 10.1016/0021-9991(82)90058-4.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Seven-Re learning: define the information budget

blocks.text: The existing full-field surrogate and DeepONet lessons retain their original CFD data. The new CPU exercise learns only Ghia centreline profiles at Re = 100,400,1000,3200,5000,7500,10000. A profile regressor is neither a Navier-Stokes solver nor a dense-field neural operator.

Keep every point from one Re in the same split. Inputs are normalized position t, log10(Re)-3 and a component tag. The tanh MLP enforces endpoints with u_pred(t) = t + t(1-t)N_theta and v_pred(t) = t(1-t)N_theta. Values are normalized by U. No pressure or off-centreline field is inferred.
Architecture, initialization and data weights

Compare 2 versus 5 hidden layers, width 24, Xavier initialization and seeds 7,23,61. The models have 721 and 2521 parameters; this is not a capacity-matched depth experiment. Uniform case/component weights are compared with threefold weights at t < 0.12 or t > 0.88, renormalized per case/component. These are regression data weights, not PINN PDE/boundary weights.
Here z contains the inputs, y the normalized sampled velocity, theta all network parameters, and w the fixed data weights. Audit unweighted wall and core errors even when training uses wall weights.

Data and masks: references/ghia/. Implementation: flowmllab/ghia_surrogate.py. Split, selection and model hashes: results/cavity_ghia_allre/frozen_selection.json. The disclosed tests cannot remain independent after further test-informed tuning.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Why optimizer and depth can help - and why they can fail

blocks.text: Adam combines first and second gradient moments, with componentwise products and divisions:
g is the objective gradient, alpha the learning rate, beta1/beta2 the moment-decay factors and epsilon a small stabilizer. Bias correction accounts for the initially zero moments.

L-BFGS builds an approximate inverse Hessian H_t from recent s_t = theta_(t+1)-theta_t and y_t = g_(t+1)-g_t, and takes direction d_t = -H_t g_t with a line search. Its evaluations need the same deterministic objective. Changing samples or weights inside a line search destroys that comparison.

Adam may provide a useful starting point before curvature-based refinement. More depth can represent sharper profiles but adds parameters and changes the conditioning. Wall weighting prioritizes steep near-wall structure but can damage the core. These are mechanisms to test, not universal guarantees.

Each fit used 1200 joint function/gradient evaluations. Re=400 selected the five-layer wall-weighted hybrid. It improves on Adam but loses to the interpolant on both tests. Equal evaluations are not equal FLOPs or runtime; the recorded shared-machine timings are not a controlled speed benchmark.

Staged optimization and loss conditioning: Rathore et al., ICML 2024, proceedings.mlr.press/v235/rathore24a.html. This paper motivates a test; the table above is FlowMLLab's separate measured profile experiment.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Exercises: from a better network to a better method

blocks.text: 1. Rebuild the test table from scores.csv: average u/v within each seed, then report seed mean and standard deviation. Identify which architecture/optimizer changes improve on the neural baseline and which still lose to interpolation.

2. Make an approximately parameter-matched 2/5-layer comparison. Declare seeds, learning rate, budget and weighting before training. Select only on Re=400. Add a warm-up and repeated timing if you make an efficiency claim.

3. Change near-wall data weight from 1 to 3 or 5. Report unweighted wall and core errors, signed profiles and validation loss. Explain the difference between optimizing a weighted objective and measuring uniform-domain accuracy.

4. Compare linear interpolation in Re versus log Re using validation only. Freeze the convention. The present log-Re interpolant is the baseline for the retained test table, not a claim that it is optimal for every dataset.

5. Design the full-field extension: admit CFD fields at all seven Re using mesh/time-step checks, then freeze whole-Re splits. Fit normalization and POD bases using only training fields. Compare field interpolation, POD regression and DeepONet before attributing value to a deeper network.
Research next steps with evidence boundaries

JAX-PI's cavity example motivates Re continuation, gradient-norm weighting and modified MLPs. PirateNets motivates residual connections rather than blindly adding layers. The authors' D/W=5 paper motivates regional velocity/pressure/vorticity audits and controlled SOAP/self-scaled-Broyden comparisons. None of these has been newly validated at all seven full-field Re values by the profile experiment.

Sources and exact proposed ablations: docs/CAVITY_RESEARCH_ROADMAP.md. JAX-PI: github.com/PredictiveIntelligenceLab/jaxpi/tree/main/examples/ldc. PirateNets: arxiv.org/abs/2402.00326. D/W=5 paper: arxiv.org/abs/2610.38814v2.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Mesh and time sensitivity are separate questions

blocks.caption: Finest-grid black streamlines. Automatic seeding can miss small vortices; inspect signed streamfunction contours in the corner exercise.

blocks.text: The vector mesh difference uses common native samples and is not an exact-error bound. Both temporal runs use the same 256-cell initial perturbation, dt=0.002/0.001, and tU/L=0..10. Tiny paired differences test temporal discretization, not total CFD accuracy.

The Re=10000 perturbation grows by 8.7% over this finite horizon. Neither this observation nor decay of one perturbation proves long-time stability. A steady 2-D root also need not be a stable physical 3-D flow. Pressure is not reconstructed.
Engineering task: compare signed profiles and corner extrema across all grids; state which numerical criterion fails as well as which passes.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: A full-field POD-DeepONet with whole-Re tests

blocks.text: Lab 8 learns both velocity components from our matched native CFD fields. It is supervised parameter-to-field learning, not a data-free PINN. Stack q=[u;v], compute the mean and orthonormal POD modes only from training fields, and learn the coefficients with a tanh branch.

Two and five layers, Adam and Adam-to-L-BFGS, global/per-mode coefficient scales, and a capacity-matched depth control use three seeds and the same maximum evaluation budget. Select by mean validation vector error; retain all seed outcomes.

s_k is either one common training RMS or each mode RMS. Per-mode weights emphasize weak modes but can harm optimization/generalization. More layers are not automatically better. Interpolation receives precisely the same training fields.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Representational error and held-out prediction

blocks.text: The original nine-case POD had a 3.251% projection floor at validation Re=400. Adding independent training solves at 500 and 750 addressed missing spatial content; test cases were unchanged and unscored. This validation-led amendment is retained, not presented as a fixed design chosen in advance.

Projection uses target truth and is only an oracle lower bound. It is not the neural prediction. The model, basis and test coefficients were hash-frozen before scoring. The reported neural field is the selected three-seed average.

These percentages measure the full velocity-vector discrepancy against the 512-cell CFD solution. They are not speed-only errors or proof of exact physical accuracy. The 256-to-512 sensitivities at the two tests are 2.03% and 4.72%.

blocks.caption: Signed profiles distinguish the Adam baseline, selected neural result and interpolation, alongside CFD and actual Ghia samples.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Look at the flow and where the errors occur

blocks.caption: Held-out Re=7500: CFD, neural and interpolation speed use one colour scale; the vector-error maps share a linear scale. Native samples are retained.

blocks.text: A fixed linear CFD basis preserves the common wall values and discrete continuity. Its nonlinear vorticity-transport residual is generally nonzero. Compute this residual separately: small supervised error and small divergence do not imply satisfaction of nonlinear momentum.

Inspect both centreline components, vortex structure and spatial errors. A small global norm can hide local failure; use regional diagnostics for weak recirculation. No pressure or long-time-stability claim follows from these velocity comparisons.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Engineering work: five measured comparisons

blocks.text: A. From the Lab 8 validation table, report per-Re mean and seed range for all five configurations. Compare optimizer at fixed depth, depth at fixed width, the capacity-matched control, and coefficient scaling. Identify both improvements and deterioration.

B. Compare the retained first-round and final validation errors. Explain the role of the projection floor and the two extra training fields; separate this change in information from optimizer effects.

C. For each held-out Re, report vector/component L2, maximum signed centreline error and its location. Compare the selected ensemble with both interpolation conventions. Supply physical profiles, not bar charts.

D. Compare neural error with the native mesh sensitivity and independently computed nonlinear residual. Explain why a mesh difference is not a certified error bound and exact divergence does not establish momentum balance.

E. Enable the optional CPU cell and change one architecture or optimizer setting. Keep fitting and selection on training/validation only. Published test scores are disclosed; further test-based tuning is exploratory and needs fresh withheld cases for a blind claim.

Deliverables: one CSV of measured results, two signed-profile figures, and an interpretation separating representation, optimization and CFD discretization. Record source/model/data hashes. Earlier laboratories remain available and unchanged.

Methods in context: FFV-PINN solves separate data-free square-cavity cases with finite-volume residuals and correction loss; Roohi-McDevitt assesses regional accuracy in a regularized D/W=5 cavity. Neither should be conflated with this supervised parameter surrogate. Primary-source links: docs/CAVITY_ALL_RE_NEURAL_LITERATURE.md.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Vorticity fields and signed discrepancies

blocks.caption: Each row compares CFD-derived vorticity, neural-derived vorticity and their signed difference. Re1000 is above; Re7500 below. All values are retained.

blocks.text: The four physical fields share one symmetric-log normalization, with a linear threshold of 1 in omega L/U. Each difference map has its own displayed linear scale. Do not compare error colours between rows without reading those scales.

At Re7500 the largest signed difference is +0.22715 U/L at x/L=0.99609, y/L=0.97852. The lid discontinuity makes the near-corner gradients sensitive to both discretization and surrogate error. Use the signed map and location together with the global norm.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Pressure from a common reconstruction operator

blocks.text: Starred velocity and coordinates are nondimensionalized by U and L; rho is the constant density. Centered steady momentum gradients are integrated by the same least-squares operator for both fields. One zero-interior-mean pressure gauge is fixed for each entire field.

blocks.caption: Black: CFD-derived pressure; orange: neural-velocity-derived pressure. Both Re and both methods use identical pressure contour levels.

blocks.text: Pressure is postprocessed, not a direct network output or a comparison against an independent pressure solver. Exact affine-gradient and second-order Kovasznay tests verify the reconstruction implementation. A least-squares scalar pressure cannot exactly balance a non-integrable momentum-gradient field.

At Re7500 the derived-pressure discrepancy is 0.05373%, but CFD pressure changes by 8.90% between 256 and 512 cells on matched nodes after one constant gauge alignment. Surrogate agreement does not remove this mesh sensitivity.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Pressure colour scales and numerical limits

blocks.caption: Pressure fields share one full-extrema symmetric-log scale; signed differences use the displayed linear scales. Re1000 is above and Re7500 below.

blocks.text: The pressure scale has a linear threshold of 0.02 rho U squared. No extrema are clipped and no local pressure offsets are fitted. Both methods use the same interior points; no wall pressure is extrapolated.

For Re1000 the derived-pressure discrepancy is 0.006901% and the 256-to-512 sensitivity is 1.274%. This is a training case. Retain the separate limitations from Lab 8: supervised vector accuracy, derivative accuracy, nonlinear momentum residual, grid sensitivity and stability answer different questions.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Measured experience: choosing a cavity solver

blocks.text: Question: would replacing the sparse-direct linear solve with Newton-Krylov and multigrid make our high-Re cavity calculations faster? A matched experiment answered this for our current implementation: the candidate took 1.95-2.17 times as long in the four repeated warm-case comparisons. We retain the existing production solver for these workloads.
What changed, and what stayed fixed?

Both methods solve the same discrete steady streamfunction-vorticity equations. The grid, no-slip walls and moving lid, initial field, exact Jacobian, damped Newton iteration, line search and final acceptance tests are fixed. Only the method used to obtain the Newton correction changes.

blocks.latex: F(q_k)=0\;\mathrm{at\ convergence},\quad J_k\delta q_k=-F(q_k),\quad q_{k+1}=q_k+\alpha_k\delta q_k

blocks.text: Here q collects the interior streamfunction and vorticity unknowns; F is the discrete equation residual; J is its Jacobian; k is the Newton iteration; delta q is the correction; and alpha is the accepted line-search step. The direct method factorizes the sparse Jacobian. GMRES is the Generalized Minimal Residual iterative method.

blocks.latex: \widetilde J_k=R_k J_k C,\quad M_k^{-1}\widetilde J_k z_k=-M_k^{-1}R_k F(q_k),\quad\delta q_k=Cz_k

blocks.text: R is an invertible diagonal row scaling; C is an invertible diagonal variable scaling; z is the scaled Newton correction. The preconditioner acts on the scaled Jacobian J-tilde. These transformations preserve the original correction equation.

The operator M<super>-1</super> applies one coupled geometric Galerkin multigrid V-cycle. It uses bilinear prolongation, scaled-transpose restriction, ILUT smoothing (incomplete LU with threshold dropping), and a direct solve on the coarsest grid. Invertible row and variable scaling help the linear algebra; checks against the original unscaled equations are still required.
Why record a result that did not improve runtime?

A plausible method is not automatically a practical improvement. Preserving its failed pilots, setup cost and accepted solutions makes the result reusable: future work can target the measured bottleneck instead of repeating the same unsupported assumption. This is a CFD solver experiment, not neural-network training.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Matched timings: include the cost of setup

blocks.text: The table gives median solve wall time over three repetitions per method, grid and warm case. Each trial uses one CPU core and one BLAS/OpenMP thread on the same Intel Xeon Gold 5220 node (2.20 GHz). Python 3.12.3, NumPy 2.2.6 and SciPy 1.15.3 were recorded. Paired methods run sequentially in fresh processes, in AB, BA, AB order; the two grid studies use separate cores of the same allocation.

Re=7500 starts from the same retained Re=6500 solution; Re=10000 starts from the same retained Re=9000 solution. A grid with 257 or 513 nodes has 256 or 512 cells per side. These are warm continuation steps, not cold starts. Minima, maxima and per-trial values are retained with the notebook evidence.
A separate, longer continuation test

On 257-by-257 nodes, the same 20-root path from Re=1000 to 10000 took 247.442 s with the direct method and 561.950 s with GMRES/MG: 2.271 times as long. Both start from the same retained 128-cell Re=1000 seed, interpolated to the target grid. There is only one repetition per method for this comparison.
What the timer includes

Solve time includes residual evaluation, Jacobian assembly, preconditioner construction, linear solves and line search. It excludes queueing, imports, seed generation, initial file I/O, checkpoint writes and post-run verification. A failed pilot is not a fast successful solve. Memory records are whole-process peak RSS, not just factor storage; the candidate also used slightly more memory in these runs.

The main evaluation contains 26 successful trials, forming 13 matched pairs. The same source and packed initial-state hashes were checked for every pair. Neither this timing table nor historical Ghia timings establish a universal or hardware-independent algorithm ranking.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Diagnosis: few iterations, expensive preparation

blocks.caption: 513-by-513 nodes; representative repeat 0. The original equation residual is the maximum of the Poisson and steady-vorticity defects. The dotted line is the final 10<super>-8</super> residual threshold. Both methods take four Newton steps; the candidate takes eight GMRES iterations in total.

blocks.latex: T_{\rm solve}=T_{\rm residual/J}+T_{\rm setup}+T_{\rm Krylov}+T_{\rm search/other}

blocks.text: T denotes elapsed time in each non-overlapping phase. Setup constructs the multigrid hierarchy and its incomplete factors; Krylov includes preconditioner applications. In the recorded profiling, linear_total_seconds already contains setup: do not add setup to that total again.

The strong ILUT hierarchy is rebuilt at every Newton step. Its construction accounts for 89.3-95.2% of warm solve time, computed as median setup time divided by median solve time. It makes each linear solve converge in few iterations, but the setup cost overwhelms that benefit.

The final column is a conditional cost-model calculation, not an achieved acceleration: it is the setup reduction needed to tie the direct median if all other costs remain fixed. Reusing a hierarchy can change iteration count and robustness; it needs a fresh correctness and timing test. No reuse improvement was implemented or measured here.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Check the flow before declaring a faster solve

blocks.caption: 513-by-513 nodes; representative repeat 0. Solid black: direct Newton. Dashed red: Newton with GMRES/MG. Left: vertical-centreline u; middle: horizontal-centreline v; right: signed horizontal-centreline vorticity. U is lid speed and L is cavity width. The almost coincident curves are expected, not a missing method.

blocks.text: Superscripts MG and D denote the candidate and direct solvers; i ranges over every common native grid node. Vorticity uses the analogous relative L2 norm. The complete-field audit is separate from these centreline plots.

Across five representative full-field pairs, the largest velocity discrepancy was 2.11 x 10-14 and the largest vorticity discrepancy was 1.71 x 10-14. These quantify agreement between two numerical solvers. They are not errors against Ghia observations, a continuum exact solution, or experimental flow.

A tiny nonlinear residual identifies a discrete steady root. It does not remove mesh error, prove the high-Re branch is temporally stable, or establish three-dimensional flow accuracy. Keep the existing mesh-sensitivity, Ghia-validation and temporal checks separate.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Keep the unsuccessful attempts in the record

blocks.text: Candidate settings were explored only on the smaller 128-cell pilot grid. Each setting was tried at both Re=7500 and 10000. The bounded pilot selected the fastest setting that passed both cases; the selection was frozen before any larger-grid candidate evaluation.

rows: 2 successful trials; slower than the stronger setting
2 successful trials; selected for the main evaluation

blocks.text: Fill factor controls permitted incomplete-factor storage; drop tolerance removes sufficiently small entries during factorization. A singular incomplete factor does not prove that the original PDE system has no solution. A small residual in a scaled or preconditioned system must not replace a check of the original equations.
Acceptance was not weakened to make the candidate pass

Final checks require original nonlinear max residual below 10<super>-8</super>, combined velocity relative L2 difference below 10<super>-8</super>, and vorticity relative L2 difference below 10<super>-7</super> against the retained same-grid CFD solution. These are agreement checks. The unchanged outer linear-defect gate is 10<super>-5</super>; the candidate additionally enforces an original unscaled linear-defect threshold of 10<super>-7</super>. The inner tolerances are therefore not identical.
Reproducibility without repeating the expensive work

The compact records, plots and hashes are in <link href="https://github.com/Ehsan-Roohi/FlowMLLab/tree/main/results/cavity_solver_benchmark"><u>results/cavity_solver_benchmark</u></link>. Lab 7 audits and reanalyses these records on CPU. The full archive retains inputs, all 40 trial records, frozen code, failed pilots, recovery states and representative fields. Full-grid runs are deliberate reproduction work, not a prerequisite for the exercises.

This candidate is not Ghia et al.'s coupled strongly implicit multigrid algorithm. The result evaluates one implementation on two grids. It does not imply that multigrid or Newton-Krylov methods are generally slower than sparse direct solves.

week04_cavity_surrogates_deeponet.title: Engineering exercises: learn from the evidence

blocks.text: Use the executed appendix in Week 4 Lab 7, Section 8. Lab 8, Section 9 links the result to the cost of generating CFD labels. Run All reads frozen data; it does not run the PDE solver, submit a cluster job or train a model.
A. Reproduce the performance decision

From the raw production trials, reproduce four warm-case rows: direct and candidate median seconds, min/max ranges, and the ratio candidate/direct. Audit all 13 pairs for matched seeds, source, grid, tolerance and thread count. List the six failed pilot trials separately. Explain why neither a failed short run nor the one-repeat continuation pair should be pooled into the three-repeat medians.
B. Distinguish numerical agreement from validation

Inspect both physical profiles and residual histories, then report the two maximum full-field discrepancies from the five-pair audit. State which data would be needed to claim physical accuracy, mesh independence and temporal stability. The nearly 10<super>-14</super> agreement between solvers is not a new neural-network or Ghia validation result.
C. Set an improvement target before another run

blocks.latex: T_{\rm hyp}(r)=T_{\rm MG}-T_{\rm setup}+rT_{\rm setup},\quad r_* = \frac{T_D-(T_{\rm MG}-T_{\rm setup})}{T_{\rm setup}}

blocks.text: Here r is the retained fraction of setup cost (0 to 1); TD and TMG are measured direct and candidate medians; Tsetup is median setup time. Compute 100(1-r*) for each warm case: about 53.6-57.4% setup reduction is needed just to tie the baseline under this model. Propose when a reused hierarchy would be rebuilt and which original-equation checks must still pass. Label this a proposal, not a measured speedup.
D. Keep the neural cost comparison honest

For a surrogate, write total cost as CFD label generation plus training plus per-query inference. State which of these costs this benchmark actually measured. Do not substitute a warm continuation timer for an arbitrary cold CFD solve, or infer improved prediction accuracy from faster label generation.

Submit one numerical timing/setup table, a separate failure list, annotated physical-profile observations, and a short proposed-reuse protocol. Include the evidence manifest hash and software version. A correct decision to keep the baseline is a useful engineering outcome.

week13_rectangular_cavity_pinn.title: The authors' D/W=5 cavity: a separate research notebook

blocks.text: This extension uses retained CFD/PINN fields from Ehsan Roohi and Christopher J. McDevitt's regional-accuracy study. It complements the earlier square/D=2 matrix and near-matched D=2.2 example. D/W=5 describes geometric depth; it does not mean a five-layer neural network.

rows: 121 x 605 nodes in x and h; arrays indexed [h,x]
x/W, h/W, u/U, v/U, p/(rho U squared), omega W/U
One frozen whole-interior gauge, preserved in every region

blocks.text: The portable notebook checks the bundle hash and recomputes regional errors. All retained arrays equal the original author arrays; redundant speed arrays alone were removed. It reproduces field assessment on CPU, not the complete training/optimizer/RNG history or a fresh independent-seed experiment.

The Re=1000 common-grid field is the control trajectory. The separate refined-workflow result uses a 161x801 assessment and is tabulated separately. Never substitute that number into the common-grid series or call the two grids interchangeable.

Paper: Roohi & McDevitt, arxiv.org/abs/2610.38814v2; ancillary analysis/figure code is linked there. Notebook: notebooks/week13/W13_Deep_Cavity_D5_Regional_Accuracy.ipynb. Portable assessment code: flowmllab/deep_cavity_audit.py. Data identity: data/week13_d5/README.md.

week13_rectangular_cavity_pinn.title: Weak recirculation needs regional and dimensional diagnostics

blocks.text: A streamfunction gives u = partial psi/partial h and v = -partial psi/partial x. This enforces continuity analytically but does not remove momentum or wall constraints. Sampled vorticity omega = partial v/partial x - partial u/partial h can expose errors hidden by bulk velocity agreement.
Fixed regions and velocity errors

The interior excludes 0.02 W beside every wall. Upper-left adds x/W < 0.25 and h/W > 4.75; floor regions use h/W < 0.4 or 0.65 within that interior. Use equal sampled-node weights as in the retained assessment. Moving a region boundary changes the question.

Angle brackets denote an arithmetic mean over retained points in region R; hats denote PINN predictions and unhatted fields CFD. All arrays use lid-speed units. Report absolute error, reference amplitude and their ratio. A tiny floor error alone does not establish extremely accurate relative flow.
Pressure: one gauge, two complementary parts

blocks.latex: \delta p=\widehat p-p,\quad b_R=\langle\delta p\rangle_R,\quad s_R=\sqrt{\langle(\delta p-b_R)^2\rangle_R},\quad e_{p,R}^2=b_R^2+s_R^2.

blocks.text: Here b is the signed regional offset, s the local shape RMS and e_p the globally gauged pressure RMS. Re-centering every region erases b and changes the metric. A small shape error alone does not establish a small global-gauge pressure error.

The supplied vorticity is sampled finite differences on the common grid. It is not a native automatic-differentiation versus spectral-derivative comparison. Subsampling this grid tests assessment resolution, not convergence of the underlying CFD mesh.

The notebook checks 128 retained regional values. Cancellation-level differences in nearly zero pressure means are bounded by machine precision times the regional pressure RMS. Original arrays remain exactly preserved.

blocks.caption: The CFD/PINN speed pair shares complete extrema and a symmetric-log display scale to expose the lower recirculation. The signed u discrepancy uses a linear diverging scale. These are the retained common-grid control fields; the refined workflow is a separate assessment. The notebook also shows Re=100,250,500.

u, globally gauged pressure and sampled vorticity at three actual retained heights above the floor. Each row has its own physical units and local magnitude. A small absolute lower-cavity velocity does not remove the need to inspect relative disagreement, pressure offset and rotation.

blocks.text: Exercise: choose a height in the lowest vortex, use horizontal_profile to return its nearest actual retained row, and compare signed u/v profiles. Then change the floor-region cutoff without changing any field. Explain why the norm and configuration ranking can change.

week13_rectangular_cavity_pinn.title: Optimization workflows: retain gains and losses

blocks.text: The separate 161x801 Re=1000 assessment compares Control, Soft residual, Refined and Half envelope. Control-to-refined interior velocity discrepancy decreases from 5.624% to 2.658%; globally gauged pressure RMS decreases from 0.002793 to 0.001167 rho U squared. These are retained author results, not new trials in this extension.

The ranking depends on the observable and region: Half envelope has lower interior pressure RMS than Refined in the retained table. Sampled vorticity and the upper corner retain substantial discrepancies. A workflow should not be labelled universally best from its velocity norm alone.
What the optimization history does not isolate

The study includes transferred initialization, prescribed regional collocation, residual-scaling/envelope choices and a SOAP-to-self-scaled-Broyden refinement. Prior training histories differ. Equal final-stage steps do not create an equal-total-budget experiment, and one trajectory is not a multi-seed uncertainty study. A gain cannot be assigned to one optimizer or sampling choice without a controlled ablation.
A controlled follow-up

Fix Re, geometry, lid, precision, initialization and audit samples. Compare Adam, L-BFGS and the self-scaled-Broyden route using counted objective/gradient evaluations. Freeze collocation and loss weights during a quasi-Newton line-search stage. Separately test gradient balancing, regional sampling and residual-network depth. Match parameter count where possible and include at least three seeds.

Measured tables: results/week13_d5/regional_metrics.csv (recomputed common grid) and workflow_metrics.csv (retained detailed-grid assessment), each with provenance. Original FlowMLLab Adam/SSBroyden2 training route: qa/WEEK13_PINN_MATRIX_PROTOCOL.md.

week13_rectangular_cavity_pinn.title: Student deliverables for the deep-cavity notebook

blocks.text: Table A: for every Re, report Interior and Floor_0.4 sample count, absolute vector RMS, reference RMS and relative velocity error. Verify the arithmetic and explain why a discrepancy of order 1e-9 U does not establish nine-digit accuracy or a solver noise floor.

Table B: rank the four detailed Re=1000 workflows by velocity, pressure and sampled vorticity in Interior, Upper-left and Floor_0.4. Identify an improvement and a deterioration. Keep the detailed-grid table separate from the common-grid series.

Profile study: plot signed u, v, pressure and vorticity on actual retained rows near the floor and lid. Display legends outside the curves, units and actual sample heights. Do not create a fictitious wall value from interior-only data.

Gauge experiment: add a constant 0.001 to a copy of the predicted pressure. Recompute regional RMS, signed offset and local shape; verify their decomposition. Restore the original arrays and preserve the supplied data hash.
Derivative experiment: recompute second-order sampled vorticity and repeat after subsampling by two. Explain why this is an assessment-grid sensitivity check rather than a new native CFD mesh study.

Experiment design: propose an isolated 2/5-layer architecture comparison, an optimizer comparison and a weighting comparison. Declare parameter/evaluation budgets, seeds, validation rule and independent field reference before running. Distinguish geometric depth D/W from network depth.

Submit the executed notebook, Tables A/B, four physical-profile figures and a one-page interpretation. For further sources and concrete development proposals, read docs/CAVITY_RESEARCH_ROADMAP.md. No new full-training or all-Re CFD accuracy is implied by this retained-field exercise.
